scope: Run 36: 1952 Pusan constitutional crisis adversarial follow-up and actor discovery

documents.title: FRUS XV/1 doc.138 editorial note on martial law and arrests
documents.organization: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
documents.notes: Records midnight May 24 martial-law proclamation, preceding appointments of Yi Pom Suk, Hong Pom-hi and Yun-Kyong, Seo Min-ho arrest, four additional legislator arrests, and Embassy assessment that quorum prevention was a political objective. Assessment is preserved as U.S. Embassy judgment, not neutral fact.

documents.title: Lightner telegram 1200: U.S. demand to lift Pusan martial law
documents.author: Allan Lightner
documents.organization: U.S. Embassy Pusan / Department of State
documents.notes: U.S. government requested immediate lifting of martial law in Pusan; footnote identifies UNCURK May 28 statement and UN document A/2187 pp.12-17 as primary next target.

documents.title: President Truman to President Rhee
documents.author: Harry S. Truman
documents.notes: Urges due process and no irrevocable acts. Editorial note records June 2 cabinet ultimatum: pass direct-election amendment within 24 hours or Assembly dissolution would be pursued.

documents.title: Young memorandum: possible active steps in Korean political crisis
documents.author: Kenneth T. Young
documents.notes: Separates U.S. assessment of Rhee strategy from constitutional merits; proposes removal of Lee Bum Suk and General Won among possible U.S.-backed political program. This is U.S. policy planning, not proof of Korean legal responsibility.

documents.title: Rhee to Truman on Pusan disturbance
documents.author: Syngman Rhee
documents.provenance: presidential correspondence in official U.S. documentary edition
documents.notes: Rhee says he is seeking a solution without dissolving Assembly and frames amendment obstruction as the deadlock. Later U.S. memo notes martial law lifted, amendment passed and election held in a seemingly free and uneventful atmosphere.

documents.title: FRUS policy summary after July 4 amendment
documents.notes: Describes compromise amendment as acceptable from U.S. standpoint and notes censorship lifting and new trial order for the Assemblyman sentenced to death. Useful adversarial counterweight to coercion-only narrative, without erasing prior U.S. objections.

documents.title: 국회, 국회의원 등원버스 연행사건에 대한 보고 청취
documents.notes: 신익희·김동성·소선규 보고와 45명 수난의원 명단을 포함. 백남식의 정부관계자 출석촉구 동의도 확인.

documents.title: 국회, 의원 수난사건 및 경호경찰 교체 건 대정부 질의
documents.notes: 안용대가 내무장관 출석 동의를 제기하고 여운홍이 외무장관 출석 및 방송사건 외교문제 청취를 제기. 장택상 총리가 출석해 질의응답.

documents.title: 국회, 의원 수난사건 등에 대해 국방장관 상대 질문전
documents.notes: 신익희 의장 사회, 신태영 국방장관 출석. 결론 없이 30일 국방장관·계엄사령관 재출석을 요구.

documents.title: 국회, 131명이 소집되어 개헌 정족수 확보
documents.notes: 피신·석방·출석권고 의원이 모여 131명에 이르렀고 경찰이 행방불명 의원을 찾았다는 동시대 보도. 개별 의원의 강제 여부는 이 문서만으로 확정하지 않음.

documents.title: 이범석 내무부장관 대통령 암살미수사건 기자회견
documents.author: 이범석
documents.notes: 유시태·김시현·서상일·노기용 등 피의자/관련자로 지목한 내무장관 발표. 수사기관 주장과 확정사실을 분리해야 함.

documents.title: 국회 정·부의장 선출 투표
documents.notes: 신익희 의장 재선, 조봉암·윤치영 부의장 선출. 정치파동 직후 입법부 정상화/재편의 별도 sub-event.

documents.title: 장택상 국무총리, 검열 폐지와 벽보 부착 금지 발표
documents.author: 장택상
documents.notes: 언론·공보 통제의 완화와 벽보 규제라는 행정 조치를 정치파동의 별도 정보정책 축으로 연결.

documents.title: 국가기록원 헌법이야기 제1차개정
documents.provenance: official archival exhibition linking Gazette and presidential approval records
documents.notes: Links Gazette No.654 and No.688 and presidential approval document; summarizes direct election, bicameralism, no-confidence and prime-minister nomination elements.

documents.title: 국무회의록의 재발견: 제38·39회 정부개헌안 원칙
documents.provenance: official archival exhibition of cabinet minutes
documents.notes: May 13 Rhee limits desired amendment to direct election and bicameralism; May 14 allows discussion of upper-house approval for certain appointments and cabinet adopts government amendment principles.

documents.title: 제57회 국무회의: 개정헌법도 대통령중심제로 운용 유시
documents.author: 이승만
documents.notes: Post-promulgation executive interpretation favoring a strong president-centered executive; preserved separately from the text of the amendment itself.
